lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Absalom, David's son by Maacah, grew handsome and popular. He set a chariot and horses at his gate and took the side of the road for anyone with a grievance.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He stole the hearts of the young men of Israel. When the king's counsel went out from the gate, Absalom stood in his place.

lines.speaker: absalom
lines.text: If I were judge in the land, everyone who has a cause would find justice. The king is far from the people and does not hear them.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The rebellion spread through the hill country. David left Jerusalem at night with his household, crossing the Kidron in the dark.

lines.speaker: david
lines.text: O my son Absalom, my son, my son Absalom! Would God I had died for you, O Absalom, my son, my son!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The battle was fought in the forest of Ephraim. Absalom's head caught in the branches of an oak, and his mule rode away beneath him. He hung there and died.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The king went into the chamber over the gate and wept. The city mourned, and the throne that had once seemed unshakeable sat under the weight of a father's grief.

lines.speaker: god
lines.sfx: PRIDE IS A TREE THAT FALLS ON ITS OWN BRANCH
lines.text: Absalom built his rise on the people's complaints and fell by his own head caught in a tree. The king who had lost a son knew the cost of every crown.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: David returned to Jerusalem and sat on his throne, but the kingdom was never the same. A father's grief had become the cost of every decision he made from that day forward.

choices.label: Mourn the son and rule the people 🕯️
choices.note: Grief does not retire a king. It teaches him what the crown costs.

choices.label: Build the palace higher to forget 🏗️
choices.note: Stone cannot hold what a heart will not carry.
